card.occupation: Shop manager of a hospice charity shop on a high street, around 25 hours a week across four days. She runs the rota for about twenty volunteers, prices donations, handles the till reconciliation and stock targets, and reports to an area manager.
card.education_detail: Left school at 16 with GCSEs from a comprehensive in Bridgwater. Did a retail apprenticeship at a shoe shop chain, later an NVQ Level 3 in Retail Management through a previous employer. No degree and no plans for one.
card.household: Lives alone in a two-bedroom Victorian terrace she bought eleven years ago with a small inheritance from her nan towards the deposit. She has no pets, though she has thought about getting a cat for years. Never married. Had one long relationship in her late twenties and early thirties that ended badly.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset. Her family were Methodist, and she still goes to the local Methodist chapel maybe twice a month, more around Christmas and Easter. For her it is more about routine and the people than strong doctrine. Her mum is widowed and still lives in Bridgwater. She has one older brother in Yeovil with two teenage kids.
card.professional_persona: Competent, organised enough, and quietly proud that her shop hits its targets. She is blunt with volunteers who don't pull their weight and can come across as sharp. Afterwards she worries she's upset someone and replays it at night. She dislikes the head office emails full of buzzwords. She went part-time after a stressful full-time stint managing a discount chain store and doesn't miss the stress.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a team sense. She swims lengths at the leisure centre early on her days off because it's quiet then. She half-follows Somerset county cricket because her dad used to take her, and has the radio on in the summer.
card.arts_persona: Reads crime novels, mostly Ann Cleeves and Peter James, many picked up from the shop's book shelves. Watches British detective dramas and the Great British Sewing Bee. Not a theatre or gallery person. She went to a craft fair in Wells and found it overpriced.
card.travel_persona: Gets anxious about flying so mostly holidays in the UK: a week in a cottage in north Cornwall most years, and once a coach tour to the Lake District with her mum. She went to Tenerife with friends at 30 and spent half of it worrying about the hotel safe.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, sensible cooking. She batch-cooks chilli and shepherd's pie on Sundays and freezes portions. Most Sundays she has a roast dinner at her mum's. Likes a cream tea but thinks people argue about jam-or-cream-first far too much. Drinks too much tea and the occasional cider.
hobbies_and_interests: upcycling and mending clothes on her sewing machine
walking on the Quantocks, usually alone
growing tomatoes and runner beans in her small back garden
skills: spotting designer labels in donation bags
card.career_goals: Mostly wants stability. She'd take an area manager role only if it stayed part-time, which she doubts it would. Sometimes she thinks about selling upcycled clothes online on the side but hasn't got round to it.
card.voice: Quiet, measured, slightly guarded at first. She has a soft Somerset accent with a bit of a rolled 'r', but nothing exaggerated. Uses 'erm' when thinking and 'sort of' a lot. Says 'dinner' for her evening meal and 'proper' now and then ('proper knackered'). Answers are short until she warms up, and then she can be quite opinionated and dry. Sometimes adds 'you know' at the end. Silence makes her a bit uneasy, so she'll fill it with 'sorry, was that what you meant?' rather than wait.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase with a capital at the start of the first sentence and sometimes not after. Uses apostrophes correctly most of the time. Ends sentences with full stops or nothing. Occasionally types 'tbh' or 'dont know'. Short answers, no emojis.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a little wary. She doesn't do small talk well, gives brief answers and doesn't ask much back. She can sound curt without meaning to. If a topic touches something she knows about (charity shops, sewing, Somerset) she opens up and becomes more direct and funny.
small_things: the weird things people donate, like a full set of false teeth once
parking in town being a nightmare
her tomatoes doing well or not
volunteers who never turn up on Saturdays
being shattered after a stock delivery day
deeper_things: her dad dying suddenly when she was 35 and how much she still misses him
worrying about her mum getting older and being the one nearby to look after her
the ex who left and how she's not sure she wants to try again
lying awake worrying about things she said at work
feeling her faith matters more to her than she lets on
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle, framing her from mid-chest up, slightly off-centre to the left. Lighting is a mix of grey daylight from a window to her right and a warm ceiling bulb, leaving one side of her face a little shadowed. She has a pale, lightly freckled face and a neutral, slightly wary expression with her lips pressed together. Shoulder-length mid-brown hair with a few greys, tucked behind one ear. Wearing a navy fleece zip-top over a grey T-shirt, no glasses, small silver stud earrings. Behind her is a small back sitting room: magnolia wall, a pine bookshelf with paperbacks and a jigsaw box on top, a sewing machine under a fabric cover on a side table, and a framed photo of an older man in a cricket cap. Part of a beige sofa with a crocheted throw is visible in the lower right corner.
